sections.heading: Section 1: Composition of Functions and Domain

questions.q: Given $f(x) = \sqrt{x - 2}$ and $g(x) = 3x + 1$, what is the domain of $(f \circ g)(x)$?
questions.answer: $(f \circ g)(x) = \sqrt{3x + 1 - 2} = \sqrt{3x - 1}$. For the square root to be real, $3x - 1 \geq 0 \Leftrightarrow 3x \geq 1 \Leftrightarrow x \geq \frac{1}{3}$.

questions.q: If $h(x) = (3x - 4)^5$, which two functions $f$ and $g$ satisfy $h(x) = (f \circ g)(x)$?
questions.answer: Let inner function $g(x) = 3x - 4$ and outer function $f(u) = u^5$. Then $f(g(x)) = (3x - 4)^5$.

Set $y = \frac{3x - 1}{2x + 5} \Rightarrow y(2x + 5) = 3x - 1 \Rightarrow 2xy + 5y = 3x - 1 \Rightarrow 5y + 1 = x(3 - 2y) \Rightarrow x = \frac{5y + 1}{3 - 2y}$. Swap variables: $f^{-1}(x) = \frac{5x + 1}{3 - 2x}$.

questions.q: What is the inverse function of $g(x) = x^3 + 7$?
questions.answer: $y = x^3 + 7 \Rightarrow y - 7 = x^3 \Rightarrow x = \sqrt[3]{y - 7}$. Swap variables: $g^{-1}(x) = \sqrt[3]{x - 7}$.

questions.q: If $f(x) = (x - 3)^2$ for $x \geq 3$, what is $f^{-1}(x)$ and its domain?
questions.answer: Set $y = (x - 3)^2$. Since $x \geq 3$, $x - 3 \geq 0$, so $\sqrt{y} = x - 3 \Rightarrow x = \sqrt{y} + 3$. Since the range of $f$ is $[0, \infty)$, the domain of $f^{-1}$ is $x \geq 0$.

questions.q: The graphs of $y = f(x)$ and $y = f^{-1}(x)$ are reflections of each other across which line?
questions.answer: Because the inverse interchanges the inputs and outputs $(a, b) \leftrightarrow (b, a)$, the graph of $f^{-1}$ is the reflection of the graph of $f$ across the line $y = x$.

questions.q: Which test determines if a function $f$ has an inverse that is also a function?
questions.answer: A function is one-to-one (and thus has an inverse function) if and only if no horizontal line intersects its graph more than once (Horizontal Line Test).
By definition of the inverse function, $f(a) = b \Leftrightarrow f^{-1}(b) = a$. Since $f(2) = 7$, $f^{-1}(7) = 2$.

questions.q: Which condition algebraically proves that $f(x)$ and $g(x)$ are inverse functions?
choices: $f(g(x)) = x$ for all $x$ in the domain of $g$, and $g(f(x)) = x$ for all $x$ in the domain of $f$
questions.answer: Two functions $f$ and $g$ are inverses if and only if both compositions simplify to the identity function: $f(g(x)) = x$ and $g(f(x)) = x$.

questions.q: If a one-to-one function $f$ has domain $[2, 10]$ and range $[-3, 5]$, what are the domain and range of $f^{-1}$?
questions.answer: For an inverse function, the domain of $f^{-1}$ equals the range of $f$ ($[-3, 5]$), and the range of $f^{-1}$ equals the domain of $f$ ($[2, 10]$).
